status: B7 data set (15 November 2026): the airborne sensors of the 1985 air battle by type and year (docs/air_battle/03_PERCEPTION.md section 4, 07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 5.2). Draft. A radar names its EM RadarDef in data/em/fighter_radars_1985.json; ranges are metres against the stated target.
source: airwar_ru; dubrov_1983; lambeth_1984; nato_radar_refs; docs/research/air_battle_2026-11/aam_weapons.md and perception.md
notes: An entry needs a year; a sensor the research has no year for is a slot (below), out of every war until a source fills it. placeholder: true marks figures that are SAM3D's estimates until a source is found. The warning receivers' display behaviour (03_PERCEPTION.md 3.2) is B3's and joins this file; here only which type carries which set from which year.

sensors.name: Sapfir-23ML radar
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23ML: built for the Soviet air force 1976-81 and for export to 1985; 85 km on paper; 50-55 km with the pilot searching by hand; 80-85 km under automatic ground guidance; lock head-on at 30-50 km)
sensors.notes: The by-hand range is the radar's anchor; under ground control the controller's cue narrows the search to a sector and height band and the range becomes the cued figure (07_AIR_TO_AIR.md 5.2), with no change to the radar equation. The target (5 m2, Pd 0.5) is SAM3D's reading of 'a typical target'.

sensors.name: Sapfir-23MLA-2 radar
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23MLD: series production from 1984; the Sapfir-23MLA-2 radar)
sensors.notes: As the ML's until a source gives the MLA-2's own figures (03_PERCEPTION.md section 4).

sensors.name: Sapfir-23D radar
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23M: the first Soviet series fighter radar able to work against targets over the ground; detection 55 km and lock 35 km for a typical target)
sensors.notes: The MiG-23M carries no fit in the 1985 data: the entry is for the type's history and its slot.

sensors.name: TP-23 infrared search set
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23M: an F-4 from the rear at about 20 km in simple weather)
sensors.notes: Not an EM sensor: a range from the rear, shortened by cloud between (Weather::CloudTransmission) and against the ground (a game factor).

sensors.name: TP-23M infrared search set
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23ML: detection from the rear 35 km against a clear sky)
sensors.notes: The year is the ML's first build (1976).

sensors.name: AN/APG-63 radar
sensors.source: nato_radar_refs (in service 1973 on the F-15A/B); dubrov_1983 (about 50 km against clutter, over 80 km looking up: the Soviet view); lambeth_1984 (lock on the nose to 50 nm)
sensors.notes: The 80 km look-up figure is the anchor (by_hand_m names it: a fighter's own search); the 50 km against clutter is the look-down limit the air combat layer applies with the radar's look_down_db. No NATO source for a detection range was found; the AFIT study's 24 nm is a model input (afit_1982_vid), not used.

sensors.name: AN/APG-66 radar: PLACEHOLDER
sensors.source: placeholder: nato_radar_refs for the band; the year is the F-16A's entry (estimate); the range an estimate
sensors.notes: No usable detection range found (aam_weapons.md aam-nato-13): to be replaced.

sensors.name: AN/APQ-120 radar
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23M: the APQ-120 had no look-down mode); estimate (the F-4E's first deliveries 1967-68; not in the sources read; the range an estimate)
sensors.notes: No look-down mode in the Soviet view: the radar's look_down_db is 0. The range is an estimate until a period source is found.

sensors.name: RP-21 radar: PLACEHOLDER
sensors.source: placeholder: estimate; the RP-21 and RP-22 were not found in a usable source (aam_weapons.md aam-our-01); the year is the MiG-21MF's series (estimate)
sensors.notes: To be replaced when a source is found.

sensors.name: RP-22 radar: PLACEHOLDER
sensors.source: placeholder: estimate; no usable source; the year is the MiG-21bis's series (estimate)
sensors.notes: To be replaced when a source is found.

sensors.name: TISEO telescope
sensors.source: anderegg_2001 pp. 33, 161 (TISEO on the F-4E: identification a little further out; 'late 1970s', the decade's last year taken)
sensors.notes: Identification range beyond the eye's about 5-6 km: a game value (03_PERCEPTION.md 2.1); a cue is needed to point it.

sensors.name: SPO-10 radar warning receiver
sensors.source: spo10_tulin (an intermittent tone and a light on the S3M indicator giving the direction of attack; four antenna units); airwar_ru (MiG-23ML)
sensors.notes: In service 'by the 1970s' (low confidence); the year is the ML's first build. The MiG-27, Su-24, Su-25, Su-17M3 and MiG-25BM get the SPO-10 class by SAM3D's estimate in B3's rwr_by_year, not here.

sensors.name: AN/ALR-46 radar warning receiver
sensors.source: nato_ew_refs (flown in Southeast Asia from January 1973)
sensors.notes: Which types carried it in 1985 is not established. Since B8 the MiG-23MLD carries it as its own type from 1984 (faction_warsaw_pact.json, beside the MiG-23ML with the SPO-10); rwr_by_year stays for a type refitted in service.

sensors.name: AN/ALR-69 radar warning receiver
sensors.source: gao_masad_82_23 (on the F-16 and A-10 by 1982)
sensors.notes: Contracts from 1975; the year is the first sourced fit.

sensors.name: BVP-50-60 dispensers, 60 x 50 mm LO-43 flares
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23MLD: 60 x 50 mm LO-43 flares, added for Afghanistan, 1984-85)
sensors.notes: Defeats some infrared shots; the chain's flare_rejection decides how many.

sensors.name: Lazur-SML command link
sensors.source: airwar_ru (MiG-23ML: the Lazur-SML command link; the ground's commands to the autopilot)
sensors.notes: Carries commands, not a picture. Its ranges and commands are not in the sources read.

rwr_sets.name: NATO RWR display (AN/ALR-46 and ALR-69 class)
rwr_sets.source: gao_masad_82_23 (type, the radar's range and direction of arrival on a TV screen; faults in azimuth accuracy, threat ambiguities, false alarms and detection ranges); nato_ew_refs; the display's size, the false alarm rate and the range classes are game values
rwr_sets.notes: A launch is shown only for a contact the library calls missile guidance (the Osa's command link, sa8_command_guidance). It is a bearing and a class of range, never a place (03_PERCEPTION.md 3.2).

rwr_sets.name: Pact RWR display (SPO-10 class)
rwr_sets.source: spo10_tulin (an intermittent 800 Hz tone and a light on the S3M indicator giving the direction of attack; four antenna units; the signal's character shows the radar's mode); airwar_ru; the false alarm rate and the display's room are game values
rwr_sets.notes: It tells a search from a lock and gives the quadrant of the four antenna units; no type, no range, no launch indication: a command link steady along the tracking antenna reads as a lock.

rwr_sets.name: Pact RWR display (SPO-15L Beryoza class)
rwr_sets.source: airwar_ru (SPO-15: more accurate bearings; not legible on re-reading, aam_weapons.md aam-wp-10); the bearing error and the rest are SAM3D estimates until a source gives them
rwr_sets.notes: As the SPO-10 class until a source says more; its date and its tie to the MiG-23MLD are unverified (03_PERCEPTION.md 8).
